title: HomeShield Renewal Conditions
content:
**Renewal offer.** For Homeowners Insurance under every HomeShield program, a renewal offer is sent the program's renewal offer period in calendar days before expiration.

**Coverage A at renewal.** At renewal Coverage A rises by the program's inflation guard percentage, and the result is rounded to the nearest 1,000 dollars.

**New home discount.** At renewal the new home discount drops away.

**Renewal increase cap.** The renewal premium before discounts may not exceed the expiring premium before discounts by more than the program's renewal increase cap percentage.

**Overdue balance.** A policy with an overdue balance at expiration is not renewed. A policy that reaches expiration without a renewal ends as non-renewed, with its end date on the expiration date.

**Term.** A renewal starts a new one-year term with a new expiration date.

## Worked figures (all inputs hypothetical)

**Coverage A with a 4 percent inflation guard.** Expiring Coverage A of 412,300 dollars rises by 4 percent, that is by 16,492, to 428,792 dollars, which rounds to the nearest 1,000 as 429,000 dollars.

**Coverage A with a 6 percent inflation guard.** Expiring Coverage A of 1,250,000 dollars rises by 6 percent, that is by 75,000, to 1,325,000 dollars, already a whole 1,000.

**Increase cap of 15 percent.** Expiring premium before discounts of 1,500.00 dollars: 15 percent of it is 225.00, so the renewal premium before discounts may not be more than 1,725.00 dollars. A renewal premium before discounts of 1,700.00 dollars is within the cap; one of 1,780.00 dollars exceeds it.

The cap is measured on premiums before discounts on both sides: the expiring premium before discounts and the renewal premium before discounts.

## Points of judgement

| Situation at expiration | Renewal |
|---|---|
| Overdue balance on the policy | Not renewed |
| Policy renewing | New home discount no longer applies; Coverage A raised by the inflation guard and rounded to the nearest 1,000 dollars |
